feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. Iteration 0 (40 mm span, 12 mm footprint, y 0.05, kp 4) gave oval progress 0.664 and score 159.7, the best so far. Iteration 3 (60 mm span, 12 mm footprint, kp 6) gave oval progress 0.275 and score 112.9, using the same footprint and lead. That contrast is the strongest evidence that span drives progress. Iteration 2 (60 mm, 16 mm) gave 0.405, so footprint matters less than span. Iteration 1 showed that y 0.03 collapses progress, so keep y 0.05. Your question about kp: I did not scale kp up to 6 at 50 mm. I used kp 4.5 because the 60 mm kp 6 setting in iteration 3 did not help progress. max_error has stayed at 0.062 to 0.065 m in every iteration, so span, footprint and lead do not fix it. Decide from the next race as follows. If oval progress rises to about 0.55 or higher with line losses near 1 to 1.4, span is controlling: keep 50 mm, or move toward 40 mm if progress is still rising. If progress is between about 0.4 and 0.55, the span effect is partial: keep 50 mm and change the controller before the geometry. If progress stays at or below about 0.4, span is not monotonic, so return to 40 mm and address max_error with wheel_track.
requested_changes: If oval progress is 0.55 or higher with line losses near 1 to 1.4, move the span to 40 mm (x = -0.02, -0.01, 0, 0.01, 0.02) at 12 mm footprint and y 0.05, since iteration 0 gave the best progress at 40 mm.

If oval progress is at or below about 0.4 while line losses stay near 1, keep the 40 mm span from iteration 0 and set wheel_track to 0.10 with no other geometry change. max_error has stayed at 0.062 to 0.065 m across iterations 0 to 3, so turn rate is the untested lever.
Do not change the lead from y 0.05. Iteration 1 showed that y 0.03 cut oval progress to 0.273, and iteration 2 showed that restoring y 0.05 brought it back to 0.405.
